report.source_text: The targeted RNA sequencing by Archer FusionPlex identified an NTRK2 rearrangement joined with the novel 5' fusion partner ATG16L1. The genomic breakpoints were located in introns of the two genes, resulting in an ATG16L1 (exon 9)::NTRK2 (exon 16) in-frame fusion transcript (Figure 2A). Reinspection of the copy number alteration (CNA) plot inferred from the methylation data showed an evident loss in chromosome band 2q37.1 with a breakpoint within the ATG16L1 gene, resulting in the loss of the 3ʹ end. No apparent CNA could be seen in chromosome band 9q21.33 (NTRK2). However, zooming in on the gene level of NTRK2 hints at an copy number imbalance between the 5ʹ and 3ʹ ends, with lower levels of the 5ʹ end of NTRK2 (Figure 2B). To confirm the results, interphase fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) analysis with an NTRK2 break-apart probe was performed, verifying a DNA rearrangement of NTRK2 (Figure 2C).

report.source_text: To confirm the histopathology diagnosis, methylation array (Infinium MethylationEPIC v1.0 BeadChip, illumina) profiling was performed on FFPE tumor tissue (tumor cell content approximately 70%; methodology as previously described16). Classification with the latest Molecular Neuropathology Brain classifier v.12.5 resulted in a calibrated match score of 0.99 with PA, and the same result was obtained with the clinically validated v.11b4 (score: 0.93; www.molecularneuropathology.org/mnp). The final diagnosis was BRAF-wildtype PA, WHO grade 1.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 7-year-old boy presented in September 2019 with personality change, visual disturbance, and vomiting. Brain MRI revealed a 5×5×7 cm intraventricular tumor extending into the temporal lobe, hypothalamus, and basal ganglia. He underwent surgical resection. Histopathology of the resected tissue showed features consistent with low-grade glioma, including small cell nuclei, few Rosenthal fibers, occasional mitoses (1 per 2 mm²), GFAP and synaptophysin positivity, and a low Ki-67 proliferation rate (4.5%). Immunohistochemistry excluded high-grade glioma and other entities (normal TP53, preserved ATRX, negative H3K27 mutation). Molecular testing revealed no BRAF-KIAA1549 fusion and no mutations in BRAF or IDH1/2 genes. Methylation array profiling confirmed the diagnosis with a calibrated match score of 0.99 for pilocytic astrocytoma. Further molecular characterization identified an ATG16L1::NTRK2 fusion (exon 9::exon 16) via Archer FusionPlex, confirmed by FISH. The final diagnosis was BRAF-wildtype pilocytic astrocytoma, WHO grade 1. Following discovery of the NTRK2 rearrangement, the patient was enrolled in the SCOUT trial (NCT02637687) in June 2022 and treated with larotrectinib. After 2 months of therapy (August 2022), MRI showed decreased tumor size with partial radiographic response per RANO criteria. The patient tolerated treatment well with Lansky performance status 90-100% and no grade 3-4 adverse events.

The patient tolerated treatment well with Lansky performance status 90-100% and no grade 3-4 adverse events.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial presentation with personality change, visual disturbance, and vomiting in a 7-year-old boy
MRI showing 5×5×7 cm intraventricular tumor with extension to temporal lobe, hypothalamus, and basal ganglia
Histopathology showing low-grade glioma features: small cell nuclei, few Rosenthal fibers, occasional mitosis (1/2mm²), GFAP+/synaptophysin+, Ki-67 4.5%
Immunohistochemistry excluding high-grade glioma: normal TP53, preserved ATRX, negative H3K27 mutation
Molecular testing showing no BRAF fusion and no BRAF or IDH1/2 mutations (BRAF-wildtype)
Methylation profiling confirming pilocytic astrocytoma with calibrated match score 0.99 (MNP Brain classifier v12.5)
Identification of ATG16L1::NTRK2 fusion (exon 9::exon 16) by Archer FusionPlex
Confirmation of NTRK2 rearrangement by FISH break-apart probe
Final diagnosis explicitly stated as BRAF-wildtype PA, WHO grade 1
Enrollment in SCOUT trial (NCT02637687) requiring measurable contrast-enhancing disease
Treatment with larotrectinib with good tolerance (no grade 3-4 adverse events) and Lansky performance status 90-100%
Partial radiographic response after 2 months of therapy (August 2022) per RANO criteria

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Low Ki-67 (4.5%), normal TP53, preserved ATRX, negative H3K27 mutation, and methylation profiling consistent with low-grade pilocytic astrocytoma
Negative testing for BRAF-KIAA1549 fusion and BRAF V600E mutation
Methylation profiling with high confidence score (0.99) for pilocytic astrocytoma classification

remaining_uncertainties: Extent of surgical resection (gross total vs subtotal) not documented in available evidence
Detailed clinical course and imaging findings between September 2019 and June 2022 not fully documented
